Dampening effect of logistic source in a two-dimensional haptotaxis system with nonlinear zero-order interaction

Zhen Chen Note: chenzhendhu@163.com Affiliation: School of Information Science &\& Technology, Donghua University, Affiliation: Shanghai 200051, P.R. China
Abstract

This paper deals with the oncolytic virotherapy model

{ut=Δu−∇⋅(u∇v)−uz+μu(1−u),vt=−(u+w)​v,wt=Dw​Δ​w−w+u​z,zt=Dz​Δ​z−z−u​z+β​w,(⋆)\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}u_{t}=\Delta u-\nabla\cdot(u\nabla v)-uz+\mu u(1-u),\\[2.84526pt] v_{t}=-(u+w)v,\\[2.84526pt] w_{t}=D_{w}\Delta w-w+uz,\\[2.84526pt] z_{t}=D_{z}\Delta z-z-uz+\beta w,\end{array}\right.\qquad(\star)

in a bounded domain Ω⊂ℝ2\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{2} with smooth boundary, where μ,Dw,Dz\mu,D_{w},D_{z} and β\beta are prescribed positive parameters.
For any given suitably regular initial data, the global existence of classical solution to the corresponding homogeneous Neumann initial-boundary problem for a more general model allowing μ=0\mu=0 was previously verified in [Y. Tao &\& M. Winkler, J. Differential Equations 268 (2020), 4973-4997]. This work further shows that whenever μ>0\mu>0, the above-mentioned global classical solution to (⋆\star) is uniformly bounded; and moreover, if β<1\beta<1, then the solution (u,v,w,z)(u,v,w,z) stabilizes to the constant equilibrium (1,0,0,0)(1,0,0,0) in the topology Lp​(Ω)×(L∞​(Ω))3L^{p}(\Omega)\times(L^{\infty}(\Omega))^{3} with any p>1p>1 in a large time limit.
Key words: haptotaxis; logistic source; boundedness; stabilization
MSC (2020): 35B33, 35B40, 35K57, 35Q92, 92C17

1 Introduction

Aim at bypassing the obstacle of drug transfer in traditional chemotherapy ([10], [6]), oncolytic virotherapy becomes an alternative treatment for cancer and it has been undergoing clinical trials (cf. [2] and [9], for instance). Very recently, in order to explore efficiency of this novel therapy, Alzahrani et al. in [1] proposed the following haptotaxis model

{ut=Δu−∇⋅(u∇v)−uz+μu(1−u),x∈Ω,t>0,vt=−(u+w)​v,x∈Ω,t>0,wt=Dw​Δ​w−w+u​z,x∈Ω,t>0,zt=Dz​Δ​z−z−u​z+β​w,x∈Ω,t>0,(∇u−u∇v)⋅ν=∂w∂ν=∂z∂ν=0,x∈∂Ω,t>0,u(x,0)=u0(x),v(x,0)=v0(x),w(x,0)=w0(x),z(x,0)=z0(x),x∈Ω,\left\{\begin{array}[]{lcll}u_{t}&=&\Delta u-\nabla\cdot(u\nabla v)-uz+\mu u(1-u),&x\in\Omega,\ t>0,\\[2.84526pt] v_{t}&=&-(u+w)v,&x\in\Omega,\ t>0,\\[2.84526pt] w_{t}&=&D_{w}\Delta w-w+uz,&x\in\Omega,\ t>0,\\[2.84526pt] z_{t}&=&D_{z}\Delta z-z-uz+\beta w,&x\in\Omega,\ t>0,\\[2.84526pt] &&\hskip-42.67912pt(\nabla u-u\nabla v)\cdot\nu=\frac{\partial w}{\partial\nu}=\frac{\partial z}{\partial\nu}=0,&x\in\partial\Omega,\ t>0,\\[2.84526pt] &&\hskip-42.67912ptu(x,0)=u_{0}(x),\quad v(x,0)=v_{0}(x),\quad w(x,0)=w_{0}(x),\quad z(x,0)=z_{0}(x),&x\in\Omega,\end{array}\right. (1.1)

with positive parameters μ,β,Dw\mu,\beta,D_{w} and DzD_{z}. Throughout this work we shall assume that Ω⊂ℝ2\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{2} is a bounded domain with smooth boundary. Here u,w,zu,w,z and vv represent the densities of uninfected tumor cells, infected tumor cells, virus particles and normal tissue, respectively. Besides random motion, the uninfected tumor cells direct their movement toward the higher densities of tissue, they are assumed to follow a logistic growth and their number could be reduced due to infection by virus, while the infected cells randomly diffuse and have a natural death; the virus is released by infected cells and it experiences diffusion and loss due to decay and infection; and the tissue is degraded upon contact with cancer cells. The readers may refer to [1] for more detailed biological backgrounds behind (1.1).
Different from standard reaction-diffusion equations, the cross-diffusion term in chemotactic or haptotactic systems like (1.1) may exhibit a destabilizing feature ([5], [19]). Previous qualitative studies on such types of cross-diffusion systems mainly concentrate on global existence ([17], [11], [22], [21], [8]) and only a few address the large time behavior of solutions ([7], [12], [20]).
In contrast to preceding haptotaxis systems, (1.1) contains a nonlinear zero-order interaction term u​zuz in the third equation that gives rise to a new challenge in analysis of this system. Although (1.1) is indeed globally well-posed ([14]), a novel critical parameter phenomenon for infinite-time blow-up was recently detected for (1.1) without any growth or sink term ([15]). Moreover, the global existence and large time behavior of classical solutions was also discussed for (1.1) provided that β<1\beta<1 and μ=0\mu=0 ([16]).
The purpose of this work is to identify the stabilization effect of the logistic dampening term in (1.1). To this end, we assume that

{u0,v0 and w0 are nonnegative functions from C2+ϑ​(Ω¯) for some ϑ>0,with u0>0, w0≢0,z0≢0, v0∈W1,2​(Ω) and ∂u0∂ν=∂v0∂ν=∂w0∂ν=0 on ∂Ω.\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}\mbox{$u_{0},v_{0}$ and $w_{0}$ are nonnegative functions from $C^{2+\vartheta}(\overline{\Omega})$ for some $\vartheta>0$,}\\[2.84526pt] \mbox{with $u_{0}>0$, $w_{0}\not\equiv 0,z_{0}\not\equiv 0$, $\sqrt{v_{0}}\in W^{1,2}(\Omega)$ and $\frac{\partial u_{0}}{\partial\nu}=\frac{\partial v_{0}}{\partial\nu}=\frac{\partial w_{0}}{\partial\nu}=0$ on $\partial\Omega$.}\end{array}\right. (1.2)

We shall prove that whenever μ>0\mu>0, for any β>0\beta>0 the classical solution of (1.1) is uniformly bounded; furthermore, it is claimed that if β<1\beta<1, then the solution (u,v,w,z)(u,v,w,z) stabilizes to the constant stationary solution (1,0,0,0)(1,0,0,0) in L∞L^{\infty} topology. More precisely, we have the following:

Theorem 1.1

Let μ>0\mu>0, and let Ω⊂ℝ2\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{2} be a smoothly bounded domain. Then for any given (u0,v0,w0,z0)(u_{0},v_{0},w_{0},z_{0}) satisfying (1.2), the solution (u,v,w,z)(u,v,w,z) of (1.1) is bounded in the sense that

supt>0{‖u⁡(⋅,t)‖L∞​(Ω)+‖v⁡(⋅,t)‖L∞​(Ω)+‖w⁡(⋅,t)‖L∞​(Ω)+‖z⁡(⋅,t)‖L∞​(Ω)}<∞.\sup_{t>0}\Big\{\|u(\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)}+\|v(\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)}+\|w(\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)}+\|z(\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)}\Big\}<\infty. (1.3)

If

β∈(0,1),\displaystyle\beta\in(0,1),

then furthermore

u⁡(⋅,t)→1in ​Lp​(Ω)for all ​p≥1\displaystyle u(\cdot,t)\to 1\quad\mbox{in }L^{p}(\Omega)\qquad\mbox{for all }p\geq 1

and

v⁡(⋅,t)→0in ​L∞​(Ω)\displaystyle v(\cdot,t)\to 0\qquad\mbox{in }L^{\infty}(\Omega)

as well as

w⁡(⋅,t)→0in ​L∞​(Ω)\displaystyle w(\cdot,t)\to 0\qquad\mbox{in }L^{\infty}(\Omega)

and

z⁡(⋅,t)→0in ​L∞​(Ω)\displaystyle z(\cdot,t)\to 0\qquad\mbox{in }L^{\infty}(\Omega)

as t→∞t\to\infty.

Let us begin with the global smooth solvability of (1.1) previously asserted in [14], together with one basic solution property.

Lemma 2.1

Let Ω⊂ℝ2\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{2} be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, and assume that (u0,v0,w0,z0)(u_{0},v_{0},w_{0},z_{0}) fulfills (1.2). Then the problem (1.1) admits a uniquely determined classical solution (u,v,w,z)∈(C2,1​(Ω¯×[0,∞)))4(u,v,w,z)\in(C^{2,1}(\overline{\Omega}\times[0,\infty)))^{4} for which vv is nonnegative, and for which u,wu,w and zz are positive in Ω¯×(0,∞)\overline{\Omega}\times(0,\infty). Moreover,

‖v⁡(⋅,t)‖L∞​(Ω)≤‖v0​(⋅)‖L∞​(Ω)for all ​t>0.\|v(\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)}\leq\|v_{0}(\cdot)\|_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)}\qquad\mbox{for all }t>0. (2.1)

∫tt+1∫Ωu2≤C\int_{t}^{t+1}\int_{\Omega}u^{2}\leq C (2.3)

3 L∞L^{\infty} estimates on uu

In this section we shall establish the boundedness of uu in L∞L^{\infty}. For this purpose, as performed in [3], [4], [17] and [11] which dealt with haptotaxis-related systems, we introduce the variable change

a:=u​e−va:=ue^{-v} (3.1)

and then in view of (1.1),

{at=e−v∇⋅(ev∇a)+a(aev+w)v−az+μa(1−aev),x∈Ω,t>0,vt=−(a​ev+w)​v,x∈Ω,t>0,∂a∂ν=0,x∈∂Ω,t>0,a(x,0)=u0(x)e−v0​(x)=:a0(x),v(x,0)=v0(x),x∈Ω.\left\{\begin{array}[]{lcll}a_{t}&=&e^{-v}\nabla\cdot(e^{v}\nabla a)+a(ae^{v}+w)v-az+\mu a(1-ae^{v}),&x\in\Omega,\ t>0,\\[2.84526pt] v_{t}&=&-(ae^{v}+w)v,&x\in\Omega,\ t>0,\\[2.84526pt] &&\hskip-36.98857pt\frac{\partial a}{\partial\nu}=0,&x\in\partial\Omega,\ t>0,\\[2.84526pt] &&\hskip-36.98857pta(x,0)=u_{0}(x)e^{-v_{0}(x)}=:a_{0}(x),\quad v(x,0)=v_{0}(x),&x\in\Omega.\end{array}\right. (3.2)

A direct testing procedure leads to the following primary inequality which will be invoked in Lemma 3.2 and Lemma 3.4 below.

Lemma 3.1

Let p>1p>1. Then

dd​t∫Ωevap≤−p(p−1)∫Ωevap−2|∇a|2+(p−1)∫Ωevap(aev+w)v+μp∫Ωevapfor all t>0.\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega}e^{v}a^{p}\leq-p(p-1)\int_{\Omega}e^{v}a^{p-2}|\nabla a|^{2}+(p-1)\int_{\Omega}e^{v}a^{p}(ae^{v}+w)v+\mu p\int_{\Omega}e^{v}a^{p}\qquad\mbox{for all }t>0. (3.3)

Proof.  From (3.2) we infer that (a​ev+w)​v=−vt(ae^{v}+w)v=-v_{t} in Ω×(0,∞)\Omega\times(0,\infty) and that

If β<1\beta<1, then we have

‖a⁡(⋅,t)−1‖L2​(Ω)→0as ​t→∞.\|a(\cdot,t)-1\|_{L^{2}(\Omega)}\to 0\qquad\mbox{as }t\to\infty. (4.22)

∫0∞∫Ω(a−1)2<∞.\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\infty}\int_{\Omega}(a-1)^{2}<\infty.

Relying on this basic decay information together with the relative compactness properties implied by (4.12) and (4.13), we use a straightforward argument by contradiction to achieve (4.22); we may refer to [15, Lemma 3.5] for details in a quite similar setting. □\Box
